title: Signals and Silence
subject: world-war-ii
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Ten entries from the intelligence side of the war of 1939 to 1945.

entries.clue: Valve machine built to attack the Lorenz cipher
System that swaps letters for other letters
British sabotage and subversion body, in initials
Codename for intelligence drawn from decrypted signals
Buckinghamshire estate that housed the British codebreakers
Rotor machine used to encode German military traffic
Dummy tank or landing craft left for reconnaissance to find
Alan whose bombe design narrowed the search
Codename given to the double agent Juan Pujol Garcia

factCards.text: Intelligence produced from decrypted Axis signals was distributed under the codename Ultra, with access restricted to a small list of recipients to protect the source.
factCards.sourceTitle: The National Archives (UK), HW series records

factCards.text: Colossus, designed by Tommy Flowers and working from 1944, was built against the Lorenz teleprinter cipher rather than Enigma.
factCards.sourceTitle: The National Museum of Computing, Bletchley Park

factCards.text: Juan Pujol Garcia, run by British intelligence under the codename Garbo, supplied the Abwehr with false reports supporting the Fortitude deception before the Normandy landings.
factCards.sourceTitle: The National Archives (UK), KV 2 files on Juan Pujol Garcia
